title: Absorbing a depth-one top gate into the second layer
statement: Let $\mathrm{data}$ be layer-2 data over $n$ Boolean variables: a family of gates, each computing a DNF formula, sharing a common positive width bound. Let $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ be a Boolean circuit whose input variables are indexed by these gates, and fix an integer $l \ge 1$. Suppose that $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ has depth exactly $1$ (a single AND or OR gate applied to literals in the gate outputs), and that each gate computes a function that is representable both by a DNF of width at most $l$ — one in which, within every term, distinct literals carry distinct variables and no literal is repeated — and by a CNF of width at most $l$. Then there exist layer-2 data $\mathrm{data}'$ of width at most $l$ and a circuit $c_{\mathrm{top}}'$ of depth $0$ over the gates of $\mathrm{data}'$ such that, for every Boolean assignment $x$ to the $n$ variables, the value of $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ evaluated on the outputs of the gates of $\mathrm{data}$ equals the value of $c_{\mathrm{top}}'$ evaluated on the outputs of the gates of $\mathrm{data}'$.
hypotheses_covered: data is layer-2 data over n (gates computing DNFs with a common positive width bound)
c_top is a Boolean circuit on the gate-indexed variables of data
l is a positive integer (0 < l)
c_top has depth at least 1 (hence depth exactly 1)
each gate has an equivalent DNF of width at most l with distinct-variable and no-duplicate-literal conditions on its terms
each gate has an equivalent CNF of width at most l
replaced:
Let $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ have depth exactly $1$ over the gates of some $\mathrm{Layer2Data}$,
where (with $0 < l$) each gate has a width-$l$ DNF and CNF representation. Then there is a
new $\mathrm{Layer2Data}'$ of width at most $l$ and a circuit $c_{\mathrm{top}}'$ of depth
$0$ over it computing the same function as $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ over the original gates.
